components.css: .ds-grid { font-family: var(--sl-font, 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif); color: var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); } .ds-grid-title { margin: 0 0 0.4rem; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-grid-title b { margin-right: 0.5rem; } .ds-grid table { border-collapse: collapse; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; border-top: 2px solid var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); } .ds-grid th, .ds-grid td { padding: 0.45rem 0.6rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sl-color-hairline, #2c3038); text-align: center; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-grid thead th { font-weight: 700; font-stretch: 82%; border-bottom-color: var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); } .ds-grid tbody th { text-align: left; font-weight: 650; } .ds-grid td > a { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; min-width: 2.75rem; height: 1.75rem; font-weight: 750; text-decoration: none; color: var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); } .ds-grid td[data-n='1'] > a { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink-1, #8eaaff) 22%, transparent); } .ds-grid td[data-n='2'] > a { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink-1, #8eaaff) 45%, transparent); } .ds-grid td[data-n='3'] > a { background: var(--ink-1, #8eaaff); color: var(--on-ink, #121419); } .ds-grid td[data-n='0']::before { content: ''; display: inline-block; width: 2.75rem; height: 1.75rem; border: 1px dashed var(--sl-color-gray-4, #5f656e); vertical-align: middle; } .ds-grid td a:hover, .ds-grid td a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); } .ds-grid-src { margin: 0.5rem 0 0; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--sl-color-gray-3, #969ca5); }

components.name: Flow Plate (Fig. 1)

components.css: .ds-flow { margin: 0; } .ds-flow svg { display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; overflow: visible; } .ds-flow text { font-family: var(--sl-font, 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 650; font-stretch: 82%; word-spacing: 0.1em; fill: var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); } .ds-flow .ds-n { font-weight: 500; fill: var(--sl-color-gray-3, #969ca5); } .ds-band { fill: var(--field); fill-opacity: var(--band-opacity, 0.55); transition: fill-opacity 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-bands:has(a:is(:hover, :focus-visible)) .ds-band { fill-opacity: 0.12; } .ds-bands a:is(:hover, :focus-visible) .ds-band { fill-opacity: 0.9; } .ds-flow a:focus-visible { outline: none; } .ds-flow a:focus-visible .ds-band { stroke: var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); stroke-width: 2; } .ds-flow figcaption { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.25rem 1.5rem; margin-top: 0.75rem; padding-top: 0.5rem; border-top: 1px solid var(--sl-color-hairline, #2c3038); font-family: var(--sl-font, 'Archivo Variable', sans-serif); font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--sl-color-gray-2, #bcc1c8); } .ds-flow figcaption b { color: var(--sl-color-white, #f1f2f4); margin-right: 0.25rem; } .ds-src { color: var(--sl-color-gray-3, #969ca5); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-band { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The site is set like a statistical yearbook for industrial ecology. Each chapter has a number and a printing ink. A running head sits above every page title. Claims appear as numbered tables and figures, each with a source line. The cover figure is a material-flow (Sankey) plate, the field's own graphic: it shows the literature flowing from IE field to AI technique, and every band links to the filtered papers.

The page is paper and ink. Dark is the default theme, a blue-black stock with near-white ink. Light is a cool white stock with near-black ink. Five printing inks (cobalt, vermilion, olive, ochre, plum) carry all colour, and each ink has two jobs: it marks a chapter, and four of them also mark an IE field. Everything else is grey. Corners are square, depth comes from rules rather than shadows, and type is narrow Archivo for anything that labels or structures and Source Serif 4 for anything to be read.

Density is that of a reference work: tight ruled tables, compact chips, reading text at a 68ch measure. The docs-site hero with a button pair and a card grid is rejected. The cover leads with the title, a lede, one primary action, and Fig. 1.
keyCharacteristics: Numbered chapters, each with its own ink, repeated on sidebar tabs, running heads and the home chapter index.
Numbered figures and tables with a caption and a "Source:" line naming the data file.
Square corners everywhere, including Starlight's own controls.
Hairline and ink rules for structure; no cards, no drop shadows at rest.
Narrow sans for structure, serif for reading, mono only for code.

rules.name: The Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: An ink means a chapter or an IE field, and the pairing is fixed: cobalt = 1 Map = LCA, vermilion = 2 Literature = EoL, olive = 3 Practice = MFA, ochre = 4 Tools = urban mining, plum = 5 Demos. Never use an ink for decoration, and never give a new field or chapter an ink already taken by a different meaning.

rules.name: The Swatch Not Fill Rule
rules.body: Outside the cover plate, an IE field shows its ink as a small square swatch (0.55 to 0.75rem) beside its label, never as a filled chip or coloured text.

rules.name: The One Hue Count Rule
rules.body: Count shading on a grid uses one ink at stepped strength (22%, 45%, solid). An empty cell is a dashed outline, not a pale fill.

rules.name: The Narrow For Structure Rule
rules.body: Anything that names, numbers or navigates is Archivo set narrow (font-stretch 72 to 90%). Anything a reader reads through is Source Serif 4. Interactive islands (.not-content) set their own text in Archivo.

rules.name: The Open Space Rule
rules.body: Narrow widths shrink the space glyph, so narrow headings, running heads, chapter titles, sidebar labels and figure text take word-spacing: 0.1em.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Tables, counts, meta lines and scores use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit flat on the stock and are separated by rules. A shadow is allowed only on a panel that floats over other content.

rules.name: The Dashes Carry Meaning Rule
rules.body: A dashed outline marks a gap (the "Wanted" tag, an empty map cell) or sets the content-type tag apart from topic tags. Don't use dashes as decoration.

dos: Do number every figure and table ("Fig. 1", "Table 1.1") and give it a caption and a "Source:" line naming the data file.
Do take colour only from the five inks and the grey ramp, following the Two Jobs Rule.
Do keep every corner square (0px), including on Starlight components you restyle.
Do separate content with rules and hairlines; use the 2px ink rule for heads and table tops.
Do set structure in narrow Archivo and reading text in Source Serif 4 at a 68ch measure.
Do mark gaps with the dashed "Wanted" tag or a dashed empty cell.
Do check every new ink use against 4.5:1 on its theme's ground, in both themes.
donts: Don't build a docs-site hero with a button pair and a card grid.
Don't round corners or add drop shadows to surfaces at rest; the facet panel is the one floating exception.
Don't use an ink for decoration, or reuse an ink for a meaning other than its chapter and field.
Don't fill an IE-field chip or set field-coloured text; use the square swatch.
Don't use dashed borders as decoration; they mean a gap or a content type.
